subject: Re: Nimbus - SLA template redlines and monthly credit cap
messages:
From: Julia Mendez <julia.mendez@nimbus.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nimbus.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA redlines and questions on monthly credit cap

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our legal and SRE teams asked us to propose a couple of modest changes to Redwood's standard SLA template before we can finalize the order. The key asks are below — we attached a marked-up copy (Nimbus_SLA_Redlines_v2.docx):

- Availability: can we move the uptime floor to 99.95% (from your standard 99.99%) for our dedicated batch workloads during the first 12 months?
- Monthly remedy: we'd prefer a fixed credit cap equal to one month's committed spend rather than a percentage-of-month cap to simplify internal accounting.
- Latency: for our primary inference route we need a p95 response window of 200ms on typical prompt sizes (we understand longer tails in burst windows).

We know these are non-standard requests — happy to discuss tradeoffs. If it helps, procurement suggested a staged approach: temporary exception for 12 months in exchange for a 10% longer contract term and a small onboarding fee.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the modified availability floor and the fixed monthly credit cap? If not, please propose alternative language we can take to our procurement team.

Thanks,

Julia
Julia Mendez
Head of Procurement, Nimbus AI
---
Attachment: Nimbus_SLA_Redlines_v2.docx (docx, 48 KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Julia Mendez <julia.mendez@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nimbus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines and questions on monthly credit cap

Hi Julia —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Short answers up front: we can be flexible, but we need to align on measurable trigger windows and a maximum financial exposure that scales with risk. A few points and a proposed compromise below.

1) Availability floor (99.95% for 12 months) — we can do a temporary exception for dedicated batch workloads only, with the following guardrails:
   - Exception window: first 12 months post-go-live
   - Scope: specific dedicated capacity pool IDs you commit to in the order form
   - Reporting: weekly availability reports and a mutually agreed runbook for root cause review

2) Monthly remedy / credit cap — we generally avoid fixed-dollar caps because they distort incentives for both parties. That said, we can offer a fixed cap option: one month's committed spend as you requested, but with a reduced remedy multiplier (0.75x instead of our usual calculation) and a quarterly true-up to reconcile large deviations.

3) Latency (p95 = 200ms) — Karthik (copied) will need to validate for your chosen model/sequence-length profile. Realistically, p95 depends on model family, quantization, and request sizing; for typical 512-token prompts on our dedicated T4-equivalent pools we can target p95 ~220–260ms. If you require 200ms strict SLAs we recommend a reserved latency tier or a latency-specific on-prem option.

Proposed next step: we can accept your redlines with edits. I've attached a short summary (Nimbus_Service_Commitments_Summary.pdf) that shows the tradeoff options (availability exception + fixed cap with reduced multiplier; or keep 99.99% availability with standard remedy). If that looks acceptable, Marissa from legal can prepare redline-friendly language and we can route a short addendum for signature.

If you want to preserve your internal ask for one-month fixed cap exactly, we'll need a signature on a 24-month term with a 15% non-refundable onboarding fee — that's the alternative. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call Friday.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Nimbus_Service_Commitments_Summary.pdf (pdf, 112 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Julia Mendez <julia.mendez@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines and questions on monthly credit cap

Hi Julia / team —

Quick operational check from infra side. The latency target is feasible with the following commitments from Nimbus:

- Model family: must be locked at onboarding (we need to know the exact open model or custom artifact).
- Max prompt size: p95 numbers assume <= 512 tokens per request and stable batching behavior; occasional spikes >512 tokens will increase tail latency.
- Reserved pool sizing: we need a committed pool equivalent to at least 2x your expected p50 throughput to guarantee p95 under bursting conditions.

If Nimbus can confirm model + typical token distribution and commit to a reserved pool (we can size this in the order form), we can target contractual p95=200ms with an operational exception clause: during the first 60 days we run a tuning period (no credit triggers unless an out-of-scope incident) to stabilize kernels and batching. After tuning, measurement and credits follow the standard playbook.

I'll coordinate a short SRE onboarding checklist and ping when I have an estimated sizing.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Julia Mendez <julia.mendez@nimbus.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@nimbus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines and questions on monthly credit cap

Evelyn —

Thanks — this is helpful and much closer to where we need to be. We spoke with procurement this morning and they prefer the fixed-cap option (one month committed spend) if Redwood will accept the reduced remedy multiplier and the 12-month availability exception scoped to the dedicated pool. They also accepted the 24-month term + onboarding fee alternative if Redwood prefers the safety of the standard availability level.

Action items we agreed on internally and propose to you:
- Nimbus confirms model family and token distribution by EOD Wednesday (we'll send a small telemetry sample).
- Redwood provides a redline-ready addendum reflecting the 99.95% exception + fixed cap (0.75x multiplier) by Thursday so our legal can review.
- Schedule a 30-min SRE sizing call with Karthik on Friday at 10am PT to lock pool sizing and the 60-day tuning window.

If Redwood sends the addendum and DocuSign link by Thursday we'll aim to execute the deal next week.

Appreciate the flexibility.

Julia
Head of Procurement, Nimbus AI
---
Quoted earlier: "If you want to preserve your internal ask for one-month fixed cap exactly, we'll need a signature on a 24-month term with a 15% non-refundable onboarding fee."
